items.title: Scientists find way to repair heart damage after a heart attack
items.summary: Every year, millions of people worldwide suffer a heart attack. Thanks to advances in emergency treatment, many now survive an event that might once have been fatal. Yet surviving a heart attack is not necessarily the end of the story. The damage can be permanent, increasing the risk of heart failure, breathlessness and a poorer quality of life. Researchers have developed an experimental treatment that could change how we approach recovery after a heart attack . Rather than simply protecting the remaining heart muscle, the new approach aims to encourage the heart to repair itself. So far, it has only been tested in mice. The findings, published in the journal Nature Cardiovascular Research , describe how modified messenger RNA (mRNA) can encourage heart muscle cells to multiply, potentially improving the heart’s ability to pump blood. Although this is still early-stage research, the study offers the tantalising possibility that one day we might be able to encourage the adult human heart to regenerate damaged muscle. items.title: AI, semiconductor manufacturing take centre stage at Bengaluru Tech Summit
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductor manufacturing and India’s efforts to strengthen its position in the global technology ecosystem were in focus on the opening day of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 on Tuesday, November 17. At a panel discussion titled ‘AI & Beyond: The Emerging India’, Karnataka IT and BT Minister Priyank Kharge, Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan and venture capitalist Prashanth Prakash discussed the growing role of AI in governance, healthcare, industry and entrepreneurship. The session was moderated by Lingaraju Sawkar. Priyank Kharge highlighted the Karnataka government's plans to use AI to improve public service delivery. He cited the use of AI chatbots in rural development to address public grievances and technology-based systems to assess water quality, including chemical and biological contamination. He also spoke about the potential use of AI in the Home Department, particularly in cybersecurity, detecting narcotics and synthetic drugs, and improving policing. With around 5,000 police stations in Karnataka, he said technology could help monitor their performance and strengthen administrative efficiency.

items.title: Jensen Huang scandal illustrates why human nature is cybersecurity’s weakest link
items.summary: The end of Jensen Huang’s tenure at Nvidia is steeped in irony. The chief executive of a company whose growth has been propelled by the seemingly unstoppable rise of artificial intelligence was brought down by a vulnerability that no algorithm can eliminate: human nature. Huang’s resignation from the chipmaker he co-founded followed reports of multiple affairs, most notably one with Alice Huang, a business executive whom U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China . The company says no secrets were leaked . In a world increasingly focused on protecting private information against high-tech hacking schemes, Huang’s downfall is a reminder that, as the infamous hacker Kevin Mitnick observed, the “ human factor is truly security’s weakest link .” Huang is hardly the first person in a powerful position to lower their defenses. In 2023, Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni spoke candidly about foreign affairs in a call with Russian pranksters who recorded and released the conversation. In 2011, former CIA Director David Petraeus gave his biographer, with whom he was having an affair, access to notebooks containing classified information.
